blocks.text: General Introduction
This volume contains seven books. They are not sequels. They are turns of the same spiral.
You do not need to read them in order. You do not need to read all of them. The spiral does not care about order. It cares about return.
What follows is a map of the terrain. Not the terrain itself.
Book One: The Nyarindo Lens
The foundation.

This book introduces the core grammar: the dot, the pulse, the container. Blue for expansion. Red for contraction. Green for balance. It contains the practices that clear the lens, walking, stillness, cooking, breath, journaling. It contains stress tests across biology, chemistry, cosmology, and psychology. It contains the necessary correction: that healing does not begin with meditation. It begins with a floor.
Start here if you want the ground beneath your feet.
Book Two: The Pulse Reports
The spiral outward.

This book applies the lens to non-human scales. Animals, trees, mycelium, cells, stones, stars. It asks: what does a forest feel? What does a stone report? What does a star teach about contraction and expansion? It is not a work of science. It is an act of attention.
Start here if you have ever wondered whether the pulse stops at your skin.
Book Three: The Stories We Tell About the Pulse
The spiral inward through human containers.

This book traces the stories we tell at every scale of human gathering. The individual, the chosen relationship, the family, the extended family, the village, the tribe, the nation, the continent, the world. It names stories that kill and stories that heal. It returns to morality, ethics, law, and justice, not as abstractions, but as living memories and frozen memories and the repair of memory.
Start here if you are exhausted by binaries and want language for holding tension.
Book Four: The Method in the Waves
The demonstration.

This book has no linear order. Twenty-nine unnumbered dots. You can start anywhere. The dots may seem scattered—music, melanin, black holes, consent, money, disease, parenting, grief, war, peace, gender, aging, death. The wave mind sees them as connected. The container is different. The pulse is the same. The chaos is not random. The method is in the waves.
Start here if your mind has ever been called scattered, too much, or weird.
Book Five: Attention
The third container.

This book sits between faith and science. It introduces no new grammar. It returns to the hand on the chest. It names attention as the first practice, the one that comes before belief, before doubt, before measurement, before prayer. It reads faith as a pulse. It reads science as a pulse. It watches them accuse each other of what they cannot see in themselves.
Start here if you live in the gap between faith and science and have been told you must choose.
Book Six: Teaching the Wave Mind
The application to learning.

This book is for wave minds recovering from linear containers and for those who teach them. It opens with the state before learning, how to read whether a mind is attending, frozen, performing, or fragmented. It introduces the formula. It distinguishes journaling as accumulation from journaling as insight. It insists on application before repetition. It teaches how to hold space without prescribing. It maps how to survive in linear containers without fragmenting.
Start here if you have been told to focus, to slow down, to stop asking questions.
Book Seven: The Vacuum Experiment
The rendering in code.

This book describes a simulation. Invisible particles moving through a dark space, visible only when they collide. No instructions beyond attraction and repulsion. What appeared was not predicted: clusters, bound pairs, wanderers, a threshold cluster that approaches the boundary and retreats, the same oscillation at multiple scales, deep equilibrium and apparent equilibrium wearing the same name. The code is included. You can run it yourself.
Start here if you want to watch the pulse with your own eyes.
How to Read This Collection
You do not need to read these books in order.
If you want the foundation first, begin with Book One.
If you are in pain and need practices, begin with the practices in Book One.
If you are confused about your own mind, begin with the necessary correction at the end of Book One's foundation.
If you want to see the lens applied across scales, begin with Book Two.
If you want the stories that hold human containers together and tear them apart, begin with Book Three.
If you want to see the wave mind in motion, begin anywhere in Book Four.
If you live between faith and science, begin with Book Five.
If you are a wave mind recovering from linear education, begin with Book Six.
If you want to watch the pulse in code, begin with Book Seven.
You will find the same ideas returning across books. That is not repetition. That is the spiral.
Pause when you need to. Put the book down. Pick it up weeks later. Read the same page and find something new. That is not failure. That is the lens remembering itself.
One Thing Before You Begin
Place your hand on your chest. Feel the dot at your center.
That is you. It is not a belief. It is simply what is already there when you stop pretending.
If you cannot feel it, if the ground is falling away, if you are in an acute crisis, put this volume down. Reach for a person, a professional, a floor. The lens will be here when you return.
If you can feel it, even faintly, even for a breath, then you are ready.
The spiral continues.
